definitions.gloss: faction; school; sect; group sharing a position
definitions.explanation: A group of people sharing a position, ideology, style, or affiliation. Used both as a standalone noun and very often as a suffix attached to a name, stance, or trait.

examples.japanese: {反対|はんたい}{派|は}が{多数|たすう}を{占|し}める。
examples.english: The opposition faction holds the majority.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{猫|ねこ}{派|は}より{犬|いぬ}{派|は}だ。
examples.english: He is more of a dog person than a cat person.

examples.japanese: {党内|とうない}の{派|は}を{超|こ}えて{改革|かいかく}{案|あん}を{支持|しじ}する{動|うご}きが{広|ひろ}がった。
examples.english: Support for the reform proposal spread beyond factional lines within the party.

notes:
Attaches as a suffix to nouns, adjectival stems, or proper names to label someone's stance, preference, or group membership. As a standalone noun it usually refers to a political or organizational faction.

COMPOUNDS:
- {反対|はんたい}{派|は}: opposition faction
- {推進|すいしん}{派|は}: proponents; pro-X camp
- {保守|ほしゅ}{派|は}: conservatives
- {犬|いぬ}{派|は} / {猫|ねこ}{派|は}: dog person / cat person
- {少数|しょうすう}{派|は}: minority
- {多数|たすう}{派|は}: majority

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {党|とう}: political party — a formal organization, larger than a {派|は}
- グループ: group — neutral; lacks the sense of shared stance
